data.name: Baihas
data.gender_notes: Baihas is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root ‘Ba-H-S’, meaning ‘to be alive, to live’ and ‘to radiate, to shine’. In Islamic tradition, Baihas is a name for a girl who is full of life, radiating joy and positivity around her. The name Baihas carries the meaning “Full of life, radiant” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Baihas usually hope their child will grow to embody full of life, radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A shining light in this world
data.etymology: Baihas belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Full of life, radiant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Baihas total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_arabic.name: بيحاس
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مشتق من بحس، بمعنى الشخص الذي يمتلك حدسًا قويًا
in_arabic.long_meaning: بيحاس هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي، مشتق من الفعل 'بحس' الذي يعني التحسس أو الإحساس الحاد. يوحي الاسم بالشخص الذي يمتلك حدسًا قويًا أو إحساسًا عميقًا، وقد ورد في بعض المراجع أنه يعني الشخص الذي يتحسس أو يتنبأ بالأشياء قبل حدوثها. يستخدم الاسم في بعض الثقافات العربية للإشارة إلى الشخص الذكي أو الحاد الإحساس.

in_urdu.name: بیحاس
in_urdu.meaning: ایک ایسا شخص جس کے پاس مضبوط حدس ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: بیحاس ایک مذکر نام ہے جو عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے۔ اس کا مطلب ہے وہ شخص جس کے پاس مضبوط حدس یا احساس ہے۔ یہ نام بحس سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے محسوس کرنا یا سمجھنا۔ اسلامی ثقافت میں، یہ نام ان شخصیات کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو ذہین، فہمیدہ اور اچھی بصیرت رکھتی ہیں۔

historical_references.reference: Baihas was an important Islamic port city located on the eastern coast of the Red Sea, known for its strategic location and prosperous trade with India, China, and other parts of the Old World. It was a major center for the transmission of Islamic knowledge, culture, and commerce, with numerous mosques, madrasas, and caravanserais.
historical_references.context: Baihas was a significant Islamic city-state and trading hub in the Indian Ocean World.

historical_references.reference: Baihas was also the capital city of the Yemeni Rasulid Dynasty (1225-1454 CE), which ruled over the western part of the Arabian Peninsula and established a flourishing maritime empire. The Rasulids were known for their naval power and control of the Red Sea trade routes, as well as their patronage of Islamic learning and culture.
historical_references.context: Baihas was the political and economic center of the Rasulid Empire in the Red Sea region.
